criterion: M3 materials (dated addition, 2026-10-10): the record of every run against evidence/m3-materials-bounds.json, failures included
written: 2026-10-10, after the runs, in the order they happened

runs.what: CPU furnaces and conservation, first run
runs.result: metal 2.87e-4 and dielectric 4.73e-4 within 1e-3; anisotropic furnace FAILED (worst |albedo - 1| 0.466); volume conservation FAILED (34x)
runs.cause: anisotropic: the compensation read the isotropic albedo at the azimuth-projected roughness, which misses the masking of light leaving along the wide axis. Volume: the test's quadrature used the refraction Jacobian inverted (Walter et al. 2007 eq. 17 gives d omega_h / d omega_o), and the furnace for light arriving from outside needs the ior^2 of generalized reciprocity
runs.fix: a 4-D table of the true anisotropic split albedo (view cosine, view azimuth, roughness, anisotropy; VNDF sampled); the Jacobian and the ior^2 factor in tests/pbr_quadrature.hpp

runs.what: CPU furnaces and conservation, second run
runs.result: every family within its bound; anisotropic 3.35e-3 (bound 2e-2); rough interface R + T within 4.3e-5 of 1

runs.what: iridescence against the spectral reference, first run
runs.result: FAILED: worst 0.322 per channel (gold-like base, film ior 1.8, 100 nm, cos 0.1)
runs.cause: the KHR_materials_iridescence text sums the Fourier series to the second harmonic; with a reflective base at grazing angles the series converges slowly. Confirmed by an independent Python mirror of both paths: 2, 4, 8, 12 and 24 harmonics give 0.322, 0.140, 0.048, 0.048, 0.048
runs.fix: eight harmonics (raw::pbr::kIridescenceHarmonics), a deliberate deviation from the specification toward the physics; the residual 0.048 is the Gaussian fit to the colour matching functions

runs.what: GPU parity on D3D12 WARP, first run
runs.result: FAILED: 23 of 24,576 values outside, worst 13x the bound
runs.cause: the float64 model itself returned negative values: the Neubelt sheen visibility first chosen is not energy-bounded (KHR_materials_sheen says so), its albedo passed 1 at grazing views and the sheen albedo scaling went negative; the f32 path then differed in sign-cancelling sums
runs.fix: the specification's Charlie visibility; the conservation grid gained the grazing views mu 0.02 and 0.05 (a tightening); at mu 0.02 the sheen table on a theta axis then read 1.049, so the sheen table moved to a sqrt(mu) axis

runs.what: GPU parity on WebGPU (SwiftShader in Chrome), first run
runs.result: FAILED: 2 values outside, worst 1.17x the bound, a narrow anisotropic lobe (roughness 0.048)
runs.cause: in-shader sin and cos of the anisotropy rotation carry about 1e-6 error on SwiftShader, which the lobe amplifies; WARP's were accurate enough (0.03x on the same case)
runs.fix: the anisotropy direction arrives as a host-computed (cos, sin) material constant, as a production material system would pass it

runs.result: CPU: every check within bound (m3-materials-energy-cpu.json, m3-materials-reciprocity-cpu.json); D3D12 WARP worst 0.459 of the bound; WebGPU SwiftShader worst 0.456; the control fails at 814x on both
worst 0.024 of the bound; informative only, not evidence
runs.note: ctest on the D3D12 build ran without RAW_NATIVE_D3D12_WARP=1 and picked the hardware adapter for about 10 s while another session held the GPU lock. A protocol breach by this session, recorded here; the measured run goes through the lock queue.

does_not_prove: Anything the bounds file lists under does_not_prove; that the tables would pass at a finer test grid than the one committed.
